clue.text: Equip pal to create ornamental work

indicators.note: creating something new from these letters means rearranging them into another word

explanation.surface: Someone fixes up a friend so the pair can make decorative craftwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliqué is decoration made by sewing cut-out fabric pieces onto a backing, a kind of ornamental needlework.

clue.text: It is not bound to appeal to readers

definitions.text: It is not bound to appeal to readers

parts.words: It is not bound to appeal to readers
parts.note: reads like a free-spirited person, but 'not bound' means without a hard cover: a thin unbound booklet aimed at the public

explanation.surface: Someone free of obligations who still tries to win over an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small unbound leaflet or booklet, typically written to persuade the people who pick it up.

clue.text: Logs in to play — action that's a hopeless endeavour!

indicators.note: letters set to play move about freely, so the words before are rearranged

parts.note: an action is a military engagement, a battle

explanation.surface: Signing on to a game turns out to be a fight you cannot win.
explanation.definitionFit: A losing battle is an idiom for a struggle that is bound to fail, a hopeless effort.

clue.text: Flan made by French who put by Argentinian red

parts.note: qui is the French word for who
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born communist revolutionary, a red

explanation.surface: A tart produced by a Frenchman, set beside a left-wing Argentine.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury open tart with an egg custard filling, a type of flan.

clue.text: Not once coming up, bypassing right flat

indicators.note: bypassing means going round, leaving out the letter that follows
in a down clue, coming up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: not once means never

explanation.surface: Someone who has never risen and keeps skipping the right apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns NEVER into REVEN; 'bypassing' then drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and flat are synonyms for a level surface with no bumps.

clue.text: Sensational story giving tingle to that female Cockney

parts.note: a tingle of excitement is a thrill
her, as a Cockney says it, dropping the H: 'er

explanation.surface: An exciting tale gives a frisson to a London woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners famous for dropping the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is an exciting novel or film full of suspense, a sensational piece of storytelling.

clue.text: Eager Nan's left cotton cloth

indicators.note: read as 'Nan has left', so those letters depart from the cloth's name

parts.note: nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing
the name Nan, with the 's standing for has

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic grandmother has left behind some cotton fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan's left' reads as 'Nan has left': NAN comes off the front of NANKEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and eager are synonyms for being enthusiastic and willing.

clue.text: Full complement of grit

definitions.meaning: the full number of people in a unit or team

explanation.surface: A complete set of sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength means both the full numbers of a force and moral toughness or resolve.

clue.text: Ardent male meeting me in passage

indicators.note: in means the two pieces sit inside the passage word

parts.note: a vent is a passage letting air or smoke out
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A passionate man runs into the speaker in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and passionate, a close synonym of ardent feeling.

clue.text: Prophet: 'Before noon you will return amazingly'

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is before noon

indicators.note: returning means the word for amazingly comes back reading backwards

parts.note: so, as in 'so good', meaning remarkably or amazingly

explanation.surface: A seer predicts that someone will come back astonishingly before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Secretly, trendy needs self-assurance

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
confidence is self-assurance

explanation.surface: Privately, the fashionable crowd crave belief in themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in confidence means telling it privately, trusting it will be kept secret.

clue.text: Old fairytale being intellectual? Not yet fully proved

parts.note: ex means former, old
a peri is a fairy of Persian tales; the setter runs fairy and tale together
mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: An old fairy story that is cerebral and still untested.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy-like being in Persian mythology, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something experimental is still at the trial stage, its worth not yet established.

clue.text: Lasses returning to big pile refuse to get dropped by mine

definitions.text: refuse to get dropped by mine

indicators.note: returning means the word for lasses reads backwards

parts.note: gals is an informal word for lasses, girls
a heap is a big pile

explanation.surface: Girls coming back to a huge stack decline to be abandoned by their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: waste from a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is a mound of waste material tipped from a mine or works.

clue.text: Not a square meal for Italians

definitions.text: Not a square meal for Italians

parts.words: Not a square meal for Italians
parts.note: a square meal is a filling one, but read literally the Italian dish is round, not square

explanation.surface: Italians are going without a proper filling meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizza is the famous round flatbread dish of Italy, so literally never a square meal.

clue.text: Small canine — greyhound perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a small pet dog kept to sit on its owner's knees
read literally, a dog that runs laps of a track, as a racing greyhound does

explanation.surface: Is a little dog perhaps a greyhound?
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dog is a small pampered pet; a racing greyhound, running circuits, is jokily a dog of laps.

clue.text: It's hot and smoky at times in Vietnam

definitions.text: It's hot and smoky at times

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that Vietnam can be hot and hazy at certain times.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as weather in Vietnam; it describes a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active Sicilian volcano, which erupts with heat and smoke from time to time.

clue.text: How agreement could be made across bridge

definitions.text: How agreement could be made across bridge

parts.words: How agreement could be made across bridge
parts.note: suggests partners at the card game, but the bridge is the nose's, which lies between a pair of eyes

explanation.surface: Bridge partners reach consensus across the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing eye to eye is an idiom for being in complete agreement; the eyes face each other across the nose's bridge.

clue.text: Bill avoids bird — one's given a close shave?

indicators.note: avoiding the name means it is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the razorbill is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family
the name Bill

explanation.surface: A man called Bill dodges a bird; did someone have a near miss?
explanation.definitionFit: A razor is the blade that gives a close shave; the question mark flags the near-miss sense.

clue.text: Like a lemur, trailing badly

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters of trailing are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lemur-like animal is lagging far behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring-tailed lemur is known for its black-and-white banded tail, so ring-tail describes it.

clue.text: Foolhardy in spots

definitions.meaning: an outbreak of red spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Reckless with pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash as an adjective means reckless; as a noun it is an eruption of spots on the skin.

clue.text: Ankle was dislocated in ballet

indicators.note: dislocated means put out of place, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A dancer's ankle was put out of joint during a ballet performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet, a specific example of the art form.

clue.text: School sandwiches used to be cut in half in station

indicators.note: sandwiching means holding the other piece between its letters

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: cut in half means only the first half of the word used is kept

explanation.surface: A school pupil's sandwiches were cut in half at the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a main London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a major railway station in London, an example of a station.

clue.text: Lasting three months beyond the prime?

definitions.text: Lasting three months beyond the prime?

parts.words: Lasting three months beyond the prime?
parts.note: the season after summer lasts about three months, and figuratively it is the time of life past one's peak

explanation.surface: Does someone past their best have only three months left?
explanation.definitionFit: Autumnal describes the season following summer and, figuratively, the stage of life after one's prime.

clue.text: Raise money — it's a risk either way

definitions.meaning: literally, to flip a coin into the air
an even chance, where either outcome is equally likely

explanation.surface: Fundraising is a gamble whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss up is to throw a coin upwards; a toss-up is a situation whose result could go either way.

clue.text: Make fewer complaints about practical demonstration

definitions.meaning: a vivid example that teaches a principle

explanation.surface: Grumble less about a hands-on display.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a striking practical example that illustrates a principle.

clue.text: Jack round with a new woman

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Jack is going about with a new girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan is a woman's first name, so any Joan is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Advantage of four-speed gears

indicators.note: of means taken from within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The benefit of a car's four-speed gearbox.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight advantage over rivals, as in having the edge.

clue.text: Fox in Scotland trapping a small creature

indicators.note: trapping means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: tod is the Scottish and northern dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: A Scottish fox catches a little animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a small warty amphibian, an example of a small creature.

clue.text: Heather, after twelve months, gets young animal

indicators.note: after places the heather word behind the time period

parts.note: twelve months make a year
ling is a common heather plant

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather, a year on, acquires a young creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is an animal, especially a horse, between one and two years old.

clue.text: See April disentangling trellis

indicators.note: disentangling means pulling letters apart and rearranging them

explanation.surface: Watch the April gardener untangling plants from a garden frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice or framework on which fruit trees are trained flat, a kind of trellis.
